somalia.summary: In a recent televised address, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the United Arab Emirates (UAE) of undermining Somalia's sovereignty by funding political divisions and establishing parallel security forces. He claimed that the UAE has signed port agreements with regional administrations in Somaliland, Puntland, and Jubaland without federal approval, which he argues threatens Somalia's constitutional order. Mohamud highlighted the contentious Berbera port deal, alleging that the UAE has developed military facilities there for strategic use by foreign powers. He also linked the UAE to Israel's recognition of Somaliland, criticizing its lack of condemnation for this decision. Despite annulling all agreements with the UAE in January 2026, Mohamud warned that the UAE's actions could lead Somalia down a path of conflict similar to that seen in Libya and Yemen. While he expressed a willingness for a respectful relationship, he emphasized that Somalia would not accept any agreements that compromise its statehood.

September 2025. Photo: UNICEF/UNI860663/Ahmed # Yemen Limited access to water, healthcare heightens risk of disease outbreaks in Ta’iz city as hostilities continue The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warns that the health, water and sanitation situation in Ta’iz city is worsening amid ongoing fighting and access restrictions in Yemen . Nearly 5,600 cases of water- and vector-borne diseases were recorded over the four weeks between 25 October and this past Sunday, according to hospital officials. This includes more than 5,300 cases of acute watery diarrhea, 230 suspected cases of dengue, and over 180 suspected cases of cholera. Officials warn that decreased access to hospitals may obscure the true scale of these disease outbreaks. Conditions on the ground raise the risk of diseases spreading, including due to lack of solid waste collection and limited access to safe drinking water. Water supplies are meeting only 8 per cent of the city's needs, as fuel shortages disrupt pumping and distribution. OCHA and its humanitarian partners stress the urgent need for safe, sustained access to fuel, medicines, safe water and health services. Road closures are worsening economic and humanitarian pressures. Truck movements into Ta’iz have reportedly fallen by 80 per cent, transport costs from Aden have risen by over 150 per cent, and journeys between the two cities now take 26 hours instead of three. Basic food basket costs are up by 75 per cent, while cooking gas prices have surged by over 170 per cent. This is making it harder for civilians – especially displaced people and other vulnerable communities – to access essentials. Elsewhere in Ta’iz Governorate, continued fighting in the Saber area has damaged homes, destroyed livelihoods and livestock, and restricted access to markets and health services. Despite the challenges, the UN and its partners continue to support people who need aid. In Ta’iz city and governorate, OCHA is coordinating with humanitarian partners to provide cash assistance and food. OCHA reiterates the need for safe, sustained and unimpeded humanitarian access, the uninterrupted flow of commercial and humanitarian supplies, and support for local responders working to reach people in need across Yemen, including in Ta’iz. # Occupied Palestinian Territory Gaza: humanitarians work to protect Palestinians from colder weather OCHA reports that teams are working to prevent further winter-related deaths in Gaza , following the death of an eight-month-old child from hypothermia last Friday. Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the Director-General of the World Health Organization (WHO), said that no child should die from the cold, noting that just a few days of rain have already flooded displacement sites, destroyed tents and left families exposed. He added that an estimated 950,000 displaced people are living in flood-prone areas, including 400,000 at extremely high risk – saying that for families who have already lost so much, a tent is often their only remaining protection and losing it leaves them exposed to cold, contaminated water and disease. Yesterday, UN agencies visited five sites in Deir al Balah where people are exposed to winter-related risks. The team spoke to people residing in inadequate shelter and facing shortages of blankets, mattresses and warm clothing. Families are also facing chronic malnutrition; poor water, sanitation and hygiene conditions; respiratory infections; and very limited access to appropriate healthcare. Food supplies are also reportedly limited. At one site, more than 240 families need to be supported with voluntary relocation for their safety because of unstable sandhills. Two other sites are in an area considered dangerous, as there is a risk of cliff collapse. Field teams have been working with communities to best prepare for winter conditions amid severe shortages of required support. Site management partners are also setting up heating points using fuel heaters. Today, the International Organization for Migration and the World Food Programme warned that critical funding shortfalls and continued access restrictions are threatening humanitarian operations in Gaza, as winter puts further pressure on vulnerable families. The agencies warned that recent gains in food security remain fragile and largely depend on humanitarian assistance. Severe winter conditions are already being felt and risk reversing these gains, damaging shelters and food supplies and leaving families even more exposed. West Bank: escalating violence imperils communities Humanitarian partners are concerned by reports that an older Palestinian woman in Jericho was killed in an attack that involved Israeli settlers and Palestinians in the West Bank, while others were injured. This is an area where dozens of Palestinians had been displaced after settlers took over homes and reportedly used live ammunition. Separately, in Hebron governorate, Palestinian families were reportedly displaced from Deir Al Hawa village last Friday following threats and intimidation by settlers who had established an outpost nearby, in August, after taking over land. Partners are mobilizing assistance for them. These incidents come amid escalating violence across the West Bank, including settler attacks, operations by Israeli forces, confrontations with Palestinians, the use of lethal force, and further displacement of Palestinian families. Palestinians across the Occupied Palestinian Territory must be protected, as required by international law, and perpetrators of violations must be held accountable. # Democratic Republic of the Congo Violence undermines Ebola response efforts OCHA says that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to expand into new areas, while growing insecurity in the east of the country is complicating efforts to bring it under control. As of 15 November, national health authorities have reported more than 11,400 confirmed Ebola cases and over 5,500 deaths nationwide. At the same time, the response continues to make progress. According to WHO, transmission has been brought under control in several of the outbreak's early epicentres, while diagnostic and treatment capacity have also expanded significantly. WHO also reports that nearly 90 per cent of registered Ebola deaths now receive a safe and dignified burial, thanks to efforts of national authorities, health workers and humanitarian partners to reduce transmission and protect communities. However, insecurity puts more communities at risk and could undermine the response. In Ituri province alone, according to local humanitarian partners, more than 70 civilians have been killed in attacks on several villages in Mambasa territory in just one week. At least 14 people remain missing, with the violence also forcing more people to flee their homes. In North Kivu, insecurity and the movement of people continue to hamper surveillance and response activities in some of the areas most affected by the outbreak. The UN and its partners continue to support authorities to respond to the outbreak and help communities affected by it. Sustained and flexible funding continues to be critical to contain the outbreak and provide life-saving assistance to people affected by violence and displacement. OCHA reiterates the need to protect civilians, ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and sustain support to bring the Ebola outbreak under control. # Somalia Climate shocks, insecurity drive displacement OCHA says that drought, flooding and violence continue to force people from their homes and deepen humanitarian needs in Somalia . The UN Refugee Agency says that more than 3.3 million people – most of them women, children and older people – are currently displaced across the country. Between January and September alone, more than 800,000 people were newly uprooted, 70 per cent of them due to drought. Humanitarian partners warn that projected El Niño-related flooding could displace hundreds of thousands more people by December. Last month alone, floods displaced more than 17,500 people and affected over 170,000. Violence in Bay and Bari regions also uprooted some 9,500 people in September and October. Displacement also puts people at greater risk of violence, exploitation and abuse – especially women and girls, children, people with disabilities and minority communities. The UN and its partners continue to support displaced people, but severe funding shortfalls are forcing cuts. * The number of people receiving food assistance fell by nearly half – from 1.1 million people in January to about 600,000 in June – mainly due to underfunding. Some 233 nutrition sites and 380 health facilities have also closed or reduced services this year due to funding shortfalls. With 2026 drawing to a close, Somalia’s US$852 million Humanitarian Response Plan is just 36 per cent funded , with slightly more than $300 million received. Without urgent additional funding, thousands more displaced families risk going without the aid they urgently need. * Donations made to UN Crisis Relief help UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs reach people in Somalia with urgent support. # Ukraine Deadly attacks damage infrastructure, cut utilities OCHA says that the latest wave of attacks in Ukraine has killed and injured scores of civilians, damaged major bridges in the capital Kyiv, and disrupted electricity, heating and water supplies. Between yesterday and early this morning, at least 20 civilians were reportedly killed and more than 100 injured, including a child, according to Ukrainian authorities. The regions of Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia recorded the most casualties – and the UN and its humanitarian partners there are providing emergency repair materials, essential supplies, and psychosocial and legal support to people affected by the latest attacks. In Kyiv, overnight strikes damaged two bridges, and nearly 320 residential buildings were left without heating. Elsewhere in Ukraine, power cuts affected some 300 towns and villages in the Rivne Region, as well as parts of eight other regions. Attacks also continue to put aid workers at risk. Yesterday, a drone struck a humanitarian vehicle as it evacuated civilians with limited mobility from Kramatorsk. The driver was seriously injured, one evacuee sustained minor injuries and other passengers suffered hearing damage. Meanwhile, the death toll from the 2 November attack on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia Region, has risen to 72, including first responders. Search and rescue operations have ended, and four people remain missing. OCHA once again calls for the protection of civilians, including aid workers. # Afghanistan UN relief chief fast-tracks funds to help families ahead of winter The Emergency Relief Coordinator, Tom Fletcher, has approved the release of $18 million from the UN Central Emergency Response Fund to support families facing severe humanitarian needs in Afghanistan as winter and the lean season approach. This funding will help more than 820,000 people struggling with rising costs and food insecurity, with winter threatening to make an already difficult situation worse. It will help provide food, healthcare, nutrition, shelter, safe water and protection services, while supporting agriculture and keeping essential services running. The allocation is part of a broader $48 million response – which also includes $30 million from the Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund – to help families prepare for winter and address urgent gaps in assistance. National and local organizations will play a critical role in the response, which will prioritize returnees, internally displaced people and the communities hosting them. Women-led organizations and female front-line workers will be particularly important so that humanitarians can continue to reach women and girls. # El Niño Drought, extreme weather deepen needs in Asia-Pacific region A new UN analysis is sounding the alarm over worsening humanitarian conditions across Asia and the Pacific region amid El Niño, with impacts expected to intensify over the next six months. The analysis – prepared by seven UN agencies – warns that drought, flooding and extreme heat are combining with rising food, fuel and fertilizer costs to deepen humanitarian needs. The impacts are expected to unfold in three waves. Drought and extreme weather are already worsening food and water insecurity for millions of people. As El Niño approaches its expected peak next month, rainfall shortages could disrupt agriculture and livelihoods, with impacts varying across the region. The situation is particularly worrying in Myanmar, the Philippines, Timor-Leste, Papua New Guinea and Tonga, where extreme weather and rising prices threaten to push more people into humanitarian need. The report estimates that 190 million children across the region are exposed to unusually dry or wet conditions, putting their access to food, safe water, healthcare and education – among other essential services – at greater risk. The UN is supporting Governments and partners across the region to prepare and respond. In Papua New Guinea, the Government – with UN and partner support – is scaling up drought assistance for at least 680,000 people, including water, food, nutrition and health support. In the Philippines, early action is underway ahead of worsening drought, with emergency funds released to support farmers and communities. somalia.summary: The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) highlights critical humanitarian crises across several regions, including Yemen, the Occupied Palestinian Territory, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Somalia, and Ukraine. In Yemen, ongoing conflict has led to severe water and healthcare shortages in Ta’iz city, resulting in thousands of disease cases, while access to essential supplies is drastically limited. In Gaza, humanitarian efforts are focused on protecting displaced families from harsh winter conditions, exacerbated by recent flooding. The Democratic Republic of the Congo faces an expanding Ebola outbreak amid rising violence, complicating response efforts. Somalia grapples with displacement due to climate shocks and insecurity, with funding shortfalls severely impacting aid. In Ukraine, recent attacks have caused civilian casualties and damaged infrastructure, disrupting essential services. OCHA emphasizes the urgent need for humanitarian access and funding to address these escalating crises and support affected populations.

Opinion Analysis Why Somalia is key to Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea gambit Opinion When Somalia’s battlefield blood becomes political currency Opinion Ethiopia’s Somaliland restraint is driven by fear, not respect Opinion Raid on Ilhan Omar’s home raises questions over Trump’s power Opinion Ethiopia’s ‘betrayal’ claim masks a bid for regional hegemony World East Africa Middle East Society News Finland blocks aid grants for Somalia over migrant returns News Somali TikToker loses bid to regain refugee status in Germany News US declines to confirm reported withdrawal from Somalia base News US military accused of trapping civilians in Somalia’s floods News Somalia cabinet approves $1.26 billion budget, down nine per cent Search Middle East News Security Somalia accuses UAE of building unauthorised military bases November 17, 2026 By Mohamed Bashir Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud delivers a televised address to the nation in Mogadishu, Somalia, on 17 November 2026. Mohamud accused the United Arab Emirates of building unauthorised military bases in Somalia, arming parallel units and waging a proxy war to undermine national unity. Villa Somalia / Handout SHARE Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp Mogadishu (Somalia Today) — Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday of building military bases in Somalia without federal approval and setting up armed units beyond his government’s control. In a televised address, Mohamud said the UAE was still interfering in Somalia, 10 months after Mogadishu cancelled its agreements with Abu Dhabi. He said Abu Dhabi was waging a proxy war and backing some regional administrations politically and financially to turn them against the federal government. “A force outside the national chain of command weakens the authority and unity of the country’s security institutions,” Mohamud said. He warned Abu Dhabi against treating Somalia as weak. “We are a nation with a constitution, a lawful government and a people determined to defend their dignity, independence and unity,” he said . Acknowledging historic ties built on Islam, culture and trade, Mohamud said the UAE had hosted thousands of Somalis and their businesses during the years of state collapse. But he said that relationship of “brotherhood and trust” had been overtaken by disputes over sovereignty. “A brother does not burn your house, does not buy your property without your knowledge, and does not divide your family,” the president said. There was no immediate public response from Abu Dhabi. The UAE, which previously trained and funded Somali troops, reaffirmed its support for Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity in a January statement with the African Union Commission. Mohamud drew a distinction between the Emirati people and their government’s policies, stressing that Somalia’s grievance was not directed at ordinary citizens. However, he accused the UAE of dividing Libya and Yemen and said it had since turned its attention to Somalia and Sudan, warning that Somalia could face a similar fate if it failed to protect its national institutions. Illegal port deals In May, Human Rights Watch reported an Emirati military presence at Bosaso airport and at a nearby base used by the Puntland Maritime Police Force. The group said the UAE had trained and funded the force, which answers to Puntland’s president. The report also traced the route of Colombian military contractors who passed through Bosaso in 2025 on their way to fight alongside Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UAE denies providing military support to the RSF. Mohamud pointed to Emirati agreements to invest in and operate the ports of Berbera in breakaway Somaliland and Bosaso in the federal state of Puntland. He said Emirati interests still managed both ports and argued that deals affecting national security required federal approval. The cabinet’s 12 January decision covered both ports and Kismayo in southern Somalia, as well as bilateral defence and security cooperation. Mohamud said Somalia had also barred Emirati military and cargo aircraft from its airspace—a measure he described as defending sovereignty, not a hostile act. Puntland, Jubaland and Somaliland rejected the decision. Puntland argued that the federal cabinet had no authority to cancel its agreements on port development and security. Somalia’s state minister for foreign affairs, Ali Omar, told Al Jazeera in January that one reason for the cancellation was the alleged passage of Yemeni separatist leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi through Somaliland on his way to the UAE. Mohamud directly addressed the Berbera incident in his speech, saying the UAE had moved a fleeing militia leader through Somali territory without federal consent. “Somali territory is not a road to be crossed unlawfully, not a commodity to be bought, and not a place to be entered at will,” he said. Calls for prosecutions Dubai-based DP World still lists Berbera among its terminals. Its subsidiary P&O Ports secured a 30-year concession in 2017 to manage and expand Bosaso. Sources told Somalia Today in September that DP World was still running the port. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991. Israel became the first country to recognise it last December, a move Mogadishu condemned as a violation of its sovereignty. Mohamud accused the UAE of playing a role in Israel’s decision, noting that Abu Dhabi had declined to sign Arab and Islamic statements condemning the step. In an October interview with Al Jazeera, Mohamud accused the UAE of encouraging Somaliland’s bid for independence. He said both countries had kept their embassies open and that Somalia was trying to repair ties. On Tuesday, he said Somalia remained open to relations based on equality, respect and full recognition of its territorial unity. Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi called for the prosecution of opposition politicians he accused of working for the UAE. He urged the government to act swiftly against militias he said the Emirates had armed. “The militias they armed should be added to the list of terrorist groups,” Fiqi said. He described the UAE as hostile to Somalia’s very existence and said the politicians he accused of helping it undermine the country posed an even greater threat. Fiqi also accused some journalists of working for the UAE. He called on the authorities to close radio stations he said the Emirates had set up in Mogadishu and revoke their licences. He named no stations. The government and the opposition remain at odds over how and when to hold national elections. Talks scheduled to begin in Mogadishu on Saturday failed to open after the main opposition alliance stayed away and called for international mediation. As former VOA journalist, and media consultant, he covers geopolitics, security, governance, and international relations. somalia.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has accused the United Arab Emirates (UAE) of constructing unauthorized military bases in Somalia and establishing armed units that operate independently of the federal government. In a televised address, Mohamud claimed that the UAE's actions are part of a broader strategy to undermine Somalia's national unity and sovereignty, particularly following the cancellation of agreements between Mogadishu and Abu Dhabi ten months prior. He emphasized that Somalia is a nation with a constitution and a government determined to protect its dignity and independence. Mohamud also highlighted historical ties with the UAE but expressed that these have been overshadowed by disputes over sovereignty. He warned against the UAE's interference, which he likened to its involvement in conflicts in Libya and Yemen. The Somali government has taken measures to restrict Emirati military presence and called for accountability regarding local politicians allegedly collaborating with the UAE.

football.summary: تجري الآن مباراة تصفيات كأس الأمم الأفريقية بين جنوب السودان وأنجولا، حيث تشير النتيجة الحالية إلى تعادل الفريقين 0 - 0. المباراة تُبث مباشرة عبر قناة beIN Sports HD 3، وتُقام في جوبا، عاصمة جنوب السودان. تغطية المباراة تتضمن تحديثات لحظية حول الأهداف، الإنذارات، والتبديلات، مع إمكانية مشاركة الجمهور في توقعات نتيجة اللقاء. حتى الآن، لم تُسجل أي أحداث في المباراة، مما يعني أن الفريقين لم يتمكنا من إحراز أهداف. سيتم الإعلان عن التشكيلة الرسمية لكل فريق قبل انطلاق المباراة بنحو 45 دقيقة. يُعتبر هذا اللقاء جزءًا من الجولة الرابعة من التصفيات، حيث يسعى كل فريق لتحقيق نقاط مهمة في سعيهما للتأهل إلى البطولة. يمكن متابعة تفاصيل المباراة والإحصائيات عبر المنصة الرياضية السعودية نيوز.

قصص رياضية الرئيسية / الكرة السعودية السنغال تلامس التأهل برباعية السودان.. ولوبي يصنع نيكولاس جاكسون، مهاجم المنتخب السنغالي، يحتفل وبرفقته الحاج مالك ضيوف، الظهير الأيسر، بعد تسجيل الهدف الأول أمام السودان، الإثنين، ضمن تصفيات أمم إفريقيا (المركز الإعلامي ـ الاتحاد الإفريقي) الرياض ـ الرياضية 2026.11.16 | 06:39 pm اقترب المنتخب السنغالي الأول لكرة القدم من حسم تأهله إلى نهائيات كأس أمم إفريقيا 2027، بفوزه 4ـ2 على مضيفه السوداني، في مباراة جمعتهما، الإثنين، على ملعب مدينة جوبا، عاصمة جنوب السودان، لحساب الجولة الرابعة من عاشر مجموعات التصفيات. وجلس الثلاثي السنغالي خاليدو كوليبالي، مدافع الهلال، وموري دياو، حارس مرمى الشباب، وكلايتون دياندي، جناح الدرعية، على مقاعد البدلاء دون مشاركة، فيما لعب مواطنهم مالانج سار، مدافع نيوم، المباراة كاملة، ودخل زميلهم ديون لوبي، لاعب وسط الاتحاد، بديلًا في الدقيقة 77، وصنع الهدف الثالث بتمريرة طويلة. وتقدم السنغاليون بهدفين سجلهما نيكولاس جاكسون، رأس الحربة، والحاج مالك ضيوف، الظهير الأيسر، في الدقيقتين 4 و22. واستطاع السودان إدراك التعادل عن طريق الجزولي نوح، وصلاح الدين عادل، لاعبي الوسط، في الدقيقتين 52 و75. وفيما كان المنتخب السوداني يبحث عن إكمال العودة والفوز، تلقت شباكه هدفًا سنغاليًا في الدقيقة 87 بتوقيع الجناح باتي مبوب، وتبعه آخر بواسطة المهاجم بول ميندي مع بداية الوقت بدل الضائع، ليحسم «أسود التيرانجا» اللقاء. وتجبر الظروف الراهنة في السودان المنتخب الملقب بـ «صقور الجديان» على اللعب خارج أرضه في مدينة جوبا. ورفع الفوز رصيد السنغال إلى 10 نقاط، وواصلت احتلال الصدارة، أمام موزمبيق صاحبة النقاط الأربع، والسودان وإثيوبيا المتساويتين بثلاث نقاط. وتتواجه موزمبيق مع إثيوبيا، الثلاثاء، لحساب الجولة ذاتها في محاولة لتعزيز حظوظهما في التأهل. وإذا فازت موزمبيق، ستضمن السنغال تأهلها قبل جولتين من النهاية، لاستحالة وصول رصيد إثيوبيا والسودان إلى أكثر من 9 نقاط. تصغير تكبير مشاركة مشاركة تابع آخر أخبار الرياضية على Google football.summary: اقترب المنتخب السنغالي من التأهل إلى نهائيات كأس أمم إفريقيا 2027 بعد فوزه على السودان 4-2 في مباراة أقيمت في مدينة جوبا، عاصمة جنوب السودان، ضمن تصفيات البطولة. سجل أهداف السنغال كل من نيكولاس جاكسون والحاج مالك ضيوف في الدقيقتين 4 و22، بينما أدرك السودان التعادل عبر الجزولي نوح وصلاح الدين عادل في الدقيقتين 52 و75. ومع ذلك، تمكن السنغال من استعادة التقدم بتسجيل هدفين في الدقائق الأخيرة بواسطة باتي مبوب وبول ميندي. هذا الفوز رفع رصيد السنغال إلى 10 نقاط في صدارة المجموعة، بينما يحتل السودان وإثيوبيا المركزين الثالث والرابع برصيد 3 نقاط لكل منهما. إذا حققت موزمبيق الفوز في مباراتها المقبلة، ستضمن السنغال التأهل قبل جولتين من نهاية التصفيات.

football.summary: أمجد قلق هو مهاجم نادي الهلال السوداني، يحمل القميص رقم 36، ويبلغ من العمر 23 عامًا، حيث وُلد في 1 نوفمبر 2003. يُعتبر قلق من اللاعبين البارزين في الفريق، ويشارك في دوري أبطال أفريقيا. الهلال السوداني لديه عدة مباريات قادمة في مرحلة المجموعات، حيث سيواجه فريق هورويا في 29 نوفمبر 2026، ثم المغرب الفاسي في 4 ديسمبر 2026، وبيراميدز في 18 ديسمبر 2026. كما سيستمر الفريق في المنافسة مع هورويا مرة أخرى في 15 يناير 2027، ويختتم مبارياته في هذه المرحلة بمواجهة المغرب الفاسي في 22 يناير 2027. يُعتبر الهلال السوداني من الأندية العريقة في كرة القدم الأفريقية، ويطمح لتحقيق نتائج إيجابية في البطولات القادمة. لمزيد من المعلومات حول اللاعب وأخباره، يمكن الاشتراك في النشرة البريدية لمتابعة آخر المستجدات.
